title: I vibecoded a puzzle game
author: Frederik77
selftext:
Here's a little puzzle game I built using the GenAI gamedev tool over on Astrocade.   
[https://www.astrocade.com/games/fuzzle-pop/01KCTN51AXB01W4F4TN3J3MFSA?sharedByCreator=cspark](https://www.astrocade.com/games/fuzzle-pop/01KCTN51AXB01W4F4TN3J3MFSA?sharedByCreator=cspark)  
  
I've tried a few different GenAI Gamedev platforms so far, and I was quite surprised with how well this worked. The AI understood my initial game concept and setup the basics for me to experiment with rules and game flow, even created the assets and polished the UI based mostly on simple natural-language prompting.

comments.author: op_app_pewer
comments.body:
That was really fun! :D
Really nice music and sec as well^^
Did Astro generate that or didnyou bring it from elsewhere?

replies.author: Frederik77
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback :) The music and sfx are also AI-generated, based on prompting about the style and mood. You get varying results based on the ai model used, but the 'smart model' on astrocade works well enough for this.

comments.author: blackwidowink
comments.body: I really like this game. Feels so simple at the start and has a nice difficulty ramping with nice variation to keep things interesting. Nice work!

comments.author: IcedCoffeeVoyager
comments.body:
This has a nice vibe to it. I’m usually quick to dislike vibe-coding. Not because I’m anti-AI use but because often the results are hit or miss, mostly miss. This was pretty good though. Love the vibe, very cozy and relaxing. The little characters are cute and the music fits the vibe. Makes for a good sort of almost idle-clicking game. 

My only criticism is it got boring after a while. I’m imagining the idle sort of feel is probably the intention so maybe it’s just ultimately not for me, since I’m more of an adrenaline junky. I just felt no pressure or sense the skill-curve was ramping up in any way. I never felt particularly challenged. That’s only going to hold my attention for so long. I may not be your target gamer though. 

Other than that, love it. Good effort!

replies.author: Frederik77
replies.body: Thanks, those are some really good observations. I agree with you on the criticism, and I'm thinking of adding a timer, and maybe also the small highlight reminders of matching sets that you see in a game like Bejewelled, both to keep a sense of urgency and nerve, so the game doesn't go stale while playing.
